Potential but some bugs. Sleepzy ranks among the best of several competing apps I’ve tried for sleep tracking.

That said, there are some bugs and things that could be improved.

The app consistently crashes when I try to access the settings views for changing either the sleep goal duration, or bedtime reminders. These are surface level features early in the user journey, and the sort of thing you should see in crash logs and fix within days. So I don’t have a great initial impression of QA…

App Store screenshots depict viewing report info in the Apple Watch app, but that doesn’t actually seem to be implemented now. You can start and snooze/end your sleep session, and with some frustration you can adjust the alarm time, that’s all.

The Watch app cannot function standalone like some others apps support, you MUST also start the phone app to track sleep.

Sleepzy seems to under-report deep phase sleep for me, often showing that I have no deep sleep at all, which I doubt. It’s not clear to me if the app uses its own algorithms for phases, or uses Apple’s phase data from my Watch as-is to be fair, Apple’s apps also report suspiciously low deep sleep for me, compared to others I’ve tried that explicitly use their own algorithms.

This isn’t a huge complaint for me, accuracy is likely to vary by individual and environment and I take it all with a grain of salt with what the technology is capable of with the signals available better to focus on larger and longer-term trends in the data.

These problems aside, I like the app overall. The UX is clean, easy to use, and responsive, the presentation of data strikes a good balance of depth and usefulness.

I can start sleep aid sounds on a Bluetooth speaker from my phone, have the app record nighttime sounds after the sleep aid has finished playing, and be woken by the Watch. Only a few sleep tracking apps I’ve tried have all these features working together properly, so kudos!

Sound recording might benefit from options for sensitivity adjustment, it has not captured very much for me yet. Based on experience with other apps, I sleep soundly, rarely snore, and my environment is fairly quiet, so I don’t believe Sleepzy is missing anything significant. But the sensitivity may be too low for some users. Other apps have captured a few more (legit) sounds, albeit they needed tweaking of a sensitivity setting to eliminate tons of false positives.

reviews.text:
Good work, it’s nice to see data on sleep patterns. I bought premium because it was recommended by a youtuber I watched and she explained how she tracked her sleep, I previously only tracked my sleep with the apple included “bedtime alarm” setting. I was worried that when I subscribed the ringtone that woke me up would be too loud and invasive but I was able to find a tone that did not wake me up with too much of a fright. This app has been very helpful given I am able to see how often I toss and turn or occasionally snore during my sleep, being able to go through recording that were picked up is very helpful to me to figure out what is the cause of my bad sleep days. I was able to figure out that I often had a bad night’s rest when my environment was more noisy than it usually was which was something I was completely unconscious of because I wouldn’t register how much noise there was at night if it didn’t completely wake me.

Though this app works wonders for sleep tracking compared to just getting an idea of how much sleep you get with Apple’s bedtime alarm, I would have to say it crashed way too often for the pretty penny I put into being able to access the content that makes the app so great. I often (even now as I wrote this) cannot even launch/open the app for who knows what reason. I will click on the icon and stare at the moon and stars icon that seems the transform into a smiling face right before it crashes without getting past the screen with the apps icon on it, I have tried turning off my wifi and launching the app, turning back on my wifi, restarting my phone with wifi enabled, restarting my phone without wifi enabled yet nothing gets me past the launch screen. I’m not sure why this happens but on the few occasions where I actually do get past this screen, the app runs pretty smoothly. The best part about this app, in my opinion is that the white noise choices seem to expand with time, I have become quite the fan of the rain and thunder sound.
Thanks for all the data, I hope that someday soon I will be able to use this app every night without failure to launch or a crash.
